3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: We were in the middle of a meeting in the Palace about our immigration policy.
3.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.GovernmentBudget"] <= -7  or  Variable["BaseGame.BlackTuesdayHappened"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.SuperpowerTradeWarHappened"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.GovernmentBudget"] <= -7  or  Variable["BaseGame.BlackTuesdayHappened"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.SuperpowerTradeWarHappened"] == true) == false)

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: The ensuing discussion quickly became heated.
4.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_Bluds"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_EmergencyDecree_Banned_Bluds"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Country_Unrest"] <= 0) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Country_Unrest"] <= 0) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn05_ReligiousHarmony_Signed"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn05_ReligiousHarmony_Signed"] == true) == false)

5.speaker: Iosef Lancea
5.text: “It just doesn't make any sense to me that a foreign citizen should come before a Sordish citizen. In Sordland!”

7.speaker: Deivid Wisci
7.text: “Immigrants are the reason our economy is not completely unsalvageable.”

8.speaker: Lileas Graf
8.text: “Well said. My analysis is also in line with this. Especially during the economic recession... We are giving Sordish jobs to migrants from other countries. What about our own people?”

9.speaker: Symon Holl
9.text: “Statistically speaking, allowing immigrants to become part of the workforce contributes to our economy. But I agree that the current situation is very nuanced.”

10.speaker: Symon Holl
10.text: “With that said, we can't just tighten our immigration policy and expect the economy to stay the same.”

11.speaker: Deivid Wisci
11.text: “Look at Agnolian immigrants in Agnland. They have revitalized the whole region and in turn, boosted the economy of the entire country. Symon can attest to that.”

12.speaker: Player
12.text: “I agree that we need to consider the economic impact of immigration.”

13.speaker: Player
13.text: “We need to modernize and reach the level of the superpowers.”

15.speaker: Symon Holl
15.text: “Our money flow should be our utmost concern, if we want to have the capability to accomplish actual change.”

16.speaker: Deivid Wisci
16.text: “Look at the superpowers. Do you see them closing off their borders? Why do you think their economies are in such good shape? They are in their current state because they welcome immigration, and use it to their advantage.”

17.speaker: Iosef Lancea
17.text: “Exactly. Our citizens should never feel threatened by foreigners.”

18.speaker: Deivid Wisci
18.text: “I am of the same mind. It is proven that immigration helps countries to develop. And we cannot just deport our current immigrants.”

30.speaker: Deivid Wisci
30.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn05_FPnT_Listened_Status"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn05_FPnT_Listened_Number"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn05_FPnT_Listened_Travel"] == true) == false

36.speaker: Deivid Wisci
36.text: “We need a decision. But before we move on...”

37.speaker: Deivid Wisci
37.text: “Mr. President. Do you have any questions about the current state of immigration?”

38.speaker: Player
38.text: “What is the current legal status of immigrants?”

39.speaker: Deivid Wisci
39.text: “Currently, all accepted immigrants are given a work permit on arrival, so that they can work and contribute to the economy of Sordland. There is currently no limit on the number of immigrants accepted. However, the number has remained stable over the past years.”

40.speaker: Symon Holl
40.text: “Despite the laws, the fact is many immigrants illegally work for corporations. That is the main issue with immigration right now. Not the immigration itself.”

42.speaker: Deivid Wisci
42.text: “Official numbers show that we have anywhere between two to three million immigrants residing in Sordland.”

43.speaker: Lileas Graf
43.text: “Even excluding the countless undocumented aliens in our midst, that is a very substantial amount. The primary issue is the strife they cause between less fortunate Sordish citizens and themselves.”

44.speaker: Symon Holl
44.text: “Including them in the workforce would benefit everybody, including unemployed Sords. More taxes means more services.”

46.speaker: Deivid Wisci
46.text: “There are three major paths they choose. The first one is the Agnland to Agnolia border. The second is the Bergia to Wehlen border, and the third is the Lorren Coast.”

47.speaker: Iosef Lancea
47.text: “Agnolians are the largest group. It's a light border over there. Although recently, political fugitives from Valgsland have been crossing the Grey Sea by boat to land on our coast.”

48.speaker: Lileas Graf
48.text: “Politically persecuted Wehzek refugees tend to use the dangerous mountain passes at the Wehlen border. Many of them also have Bludish blood. This is significantly increasing the Blud populace inside Bergia.”

49.speaker: Player
49.text: “Let's move on and see what can be done about the immigration situation.”

50.speaker: Player
50.text: “I don't have any questions. Let's move on to solutions.”
50.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn05_FPnT_Listened_Status"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn05_FPnT_Listened_Number"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn05_FPnT_Listened_Travel"] == true) == false

52.speaker: Lileas Graf
52.text: “Nonsense. If not for the unlimited amount of immigration, we wouldn't be in this state.”

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: Deivid Wisci opened his dossier stamped with the seal of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

54.speaker: Deivid Wisci
54.text: “Before we make any decisions, I have to remind you.”

58.speaker: Deivid Wisci
58.text: “During the elections, we promised to tighten immigration laws. Of course, as you know, I was and I still am against it.”

59.speaker: Deivid Wisci
59.text: “During the elections we promised to keep our immigration laws relaxed. Which I think is the right course of action.”

60.speaker: Symon Holl
60.text: “I agree with Deivid. We can turn immigration to our advantage from a financial standpoint.”

61.speaker: Symon Holl
61.text: “I see your point, Iosef but the economy certainly benefits from more immigration.”

62.speaker: Iosef Lancea
62.text: “I disagree. We are supposed to control and reduce the negative effects of immigration, like crime and subversion.”

63.speaker: Lileas Graf
63.text: “Internal order on the other hand, suffers immensely.”

64.speaker: Iosef Lancea
64.text: “We need to keep our promises and focus on our own citizens. That is what I think.”

65.speaker: Lileas Graf
65.text: “We should tighten the laws to prevent further chaos.”

67.speaker: Lileas Graf
67.text: “Advantage? You should go over the amount of disadvantages caused by immigrants. I can provide you with a report from my ministry later.”

70.speaker: Player
70.text: “If we decide to tighten immigration, what does that entail?”

71.speaker: Player
71.text: “What are the consequences of keeping our immigration policy relaxed?”

72.speaker: Player
72.text: “I am ready to make a decision.”

80.speaker: Deivid Wisci
80.text: “We would have to impose quotas and, connected to that, stricter border control.”

81.speaker: Symon Holl
81.text: “On top of allowing our economy to take a hit.”

82.speaker: Lileas Graf
82.text: “Mr. Holl. Surely the well-being of our citizens and our internal security will more than compensate for any downturn in the markets."

84.speaker: Deivid Wisci
84.text: “Aside from keeping us on the path to prosperity, modernity and continuous improvement...Not much. Our current system is good for our era. We also have the capacity.”

85.speaker: Symon Holl
85.text: “This will allow us to continue protecting investments from foreign countries, which in turn will keep our trade steady. We would be more trustworthy partners. Stability draws money.”

86.speaker: Lileas Graf
86.text: “Stability? What stability? We're already seeing clashes between our people and foreign interlopers. On the contrary, the only way we can achieve stability is through tightening our immigration policy.”

92.speaker: Narrator
92.text: Everyone leaned forward, eager to hear my response.

94.speaker: Player
94.text: “We'll tighten our immigration laws. I'll sign the decree soon, so be prepared to start working on it, Mr. Wisci.”

102.speaker: Deivid Wisci
102.text: “I am glad you made the right choice.”

103.speaker: Deivid Wisci
103.text: “It is unfortunate to see Sordland move in this direction... But I trust you have good intentions. I'll move ahead with the implementation."

104.speaker: Iosef Lancea
104.text: “We will be forced to handle new waves of migrants from Agnolia. Our border posts aren't ready.”

105.speaker: Symon Holl
105.text: “This has the chance to affect our trade negotiations with Agnolia negatively. They expect us to respect the flow of people.”

106.speaker: Lileas Graf
106.text: “Also, this will bring a new tide of refugees from Wehlen. Bergia is already a difficult region to manage.”

108.speaker: Iosef Lancea
108.text: “Anything else that needs to be said?”

109.speaker: Lileas Graf
109.text: “Not only that, we've just abandoned the native Sords who need our support the most.”

110.speaker: Symon Holl
110.text: “This will isolate us in every way. The more we are connected to the world, the better.”

111.speaker: Narrator
111.text: The ministers gathered their documents and rose from their chairs, some with frowns on their faces.

113.speaker: Deivid Wisci
113.text: “Indeed. It will be a challenge to convince these countries as they see our borders close.”

114.speaker: Symon Holl
114.text: “Not only that, we've already slighted Wehlen in the past. They might see this as a return to the '30s, which will definitely affect our negotiations.”

115.speaker: Lileas Graf
115.text: “If we are finished, I need to head off and get the Ministry to work on the new policy.”

116.speaker: Player
116.text: “The citizens of Sordland aren't forgotten. Our work for them continues.”

117.speaker: Player
117.text: “My decision is final and irreversible. Time to move on.”

118.speaker: Player
118.text: “We are not leaving Sordland unprotected. It is a logical decision.”

119.speaker: Symon Holl
119.text: “I'm against isolationism. It is the wrong path.”

120.speaker: Player
120.text: “Thank you for your contributions. Let's wrap this up.”

121.speaker: Player
121.text: “We can't let internal policy be decided by foreigners. Sordland always comes first.”

122.speaker: Player
122.text: “This is not about isolating Sordland, but protecting it.”

123.speaker: Player
123.text: “I want everybody here to get used to the new changes. This is our new direction.”

124.speaker: Player
124.text: “Let's end this discussion and get to work. There are changes to be made.”

125.speaker: Iosef Lancea
125.text: “You are wrong about this. There is a reason why this country has survived the Century of Revolutions.”

126.speaker: Deivid Wisci
126.text: “Both can be a factor in decision-making. We shouldn't forget about the immigrants who live here.”

128.speaker: Lileas Graf
128.text: “And now they will compete with foreign immigrants just to put food on their tables."

130.speaker: Lileas Graf
130.text: “I hope hard-working Sords will see this as positively as you do, Mr. President.”

131.speaker: Iosef Lancea
131.text: “Same here. Our border units need to be informed and prepared.”

133.speaker: Deivid Wisci
133.text: “I'm looking forward to the upcoming trade talks. Petr and I have been visiting Staalport and Wraclawitz in preparation.”

136.speaker: Player
136.text: “The decision has been made. Let's look past it.”

138.speaker: Symon Holl
138.text: “I'll be coming along to talk with the Economy Minister. Looking forward to the potential partnership.”

139.speaker: Deivid Wisci
139.text: “The world is entering the age of globalization. This decision will make us stay behind.”

204.speaker: Symon Holl
204.text: “We need to put our economy and the recession at the forefront.”

206.speaker: Symon Holl
206.text: “I'm sorry for losing my cool, Mr. President. I have been working day and night.”

207.speaker: Symon Holl
207.text: “I'm sorry for losing my cool, Mr. President. I have been working day and night.”

208.speaker: Narrator
208.text: I'd never seen Symon this rattled. Everyone in the room turned to him in surprise.

209.speaker: Narrator
209.text: I'd never seen Symon this rattled. Everyone in the room turned to him in surprise.

210.speaker: Symon Holl
210.text: “I am currently attempting to minimize the damage this trade war will do to Sordland."

211.speaker: Symon Holl
211.text: “I am currently looking into ways to find out how we can recover from this tragedy as quickly as we can.”

213.speaker: Player
213.text: “I am expecting good results, Symon. Do not fail me.”

214.speaker: Player
214.text: “How is it looking? Is there a way out?”

215.speaker: Symon Holl
215.text: “I will do my best, but the future of Sordish citizens is at stake.”

216.speaker: Symon Holl
216.text: “I will not, Mr. President. The future of Sordish citizens is at stake.”

217.speaker: Symon Holl
217.text: “I do not want to say anything too early, Mr. President.”

218.speaker: Symon Holl
218.text: “Thankfully, we have just started receiving financial aid from Arcasia.”
218.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.BlackTuesdayHappened"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn05_SPAid_AcceptArcasia"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.SuperpowerTradeWarHappened"] == true) == false)

219.speaker: Symon Holl
219.text: “Thankfully, we have just started receiving financial aid from United Contana.”
219.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.BlackTuesdayHappened"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn05_SPAid_AcceptUnitedContana"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn05_SPAid_AcceptArcasia"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.SuperpowerTradeWarHappened"] == true) == false)

220.speaker: Iosef Lancea
220.text: “I can't believe we're accepting financial aid from communists!”

221.speaker: Iosef Lancea
221.text: “And then what? We'll become their servants?"

222.speaker: Iosef Lancea
222.text: “What's next? Letting a child murderer buy us lunch?"

223.speaker: Iosef Lancea
223.text: “First they will place their war planes in Erlory. Then their armies will come. You will see.”

224.speaker: Iosef Lancea
224.text: “Contanan war ships in Conriat! My father will be rolling in his grave.”

225.speaker: Iosef Lancea
225.text: “I do not approve of this decision at all.”

227.speaker: Player
227.text: “I will not let you question my decisions, Iosef.”

228.speaker: Player
228.text: “I have done this with Sordish citizens in mind. Nothing else.”

229.speaker: Player
229.text: “Don't be dramatic. We need to be friendly with our potential allies.”

230.speaker: Iosef Lancea
230.text: “Allies? Sordland has no allies and never did.”

232.speaker: Iosef Lancea
232.text: “That's how they take over countries, you know.”

235.speaker: Player
235.text: “I will not let you question my decisions, Iosef.”

236.speaker: Player
236.text: “I have done this with Sordish citizens in mind. Nothing else.”

237.speaker: Player
237.text: “Don't be dramatic. We need to be friendly with our potential allies.”

238.speaker: Iosef Lancea
238.text: “Allies? With those communists? I'd rather die."

239.speaker: Iosef Lancea
239.text: “That's how they take over countries, you know.”

240.speaker: Deivid Wisci
240.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.BlackTuesdayHappened"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn05_SPAid_AcceptUnitedContana"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn05_SPAid_AcceptArcasia"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.SuperpowerTradeWarHappened"] == true) == false)

241.speaker: Deivid Wisci
241.text: “Can we please get back on topic?”

243.speaker: Lileas Graf
243.text: “Well said, Mr. Lancea. We can't be naive.”

244.speaker: Lileas Graf
244.text: “Mr. Lancea has a point. We have seen it happen many times.”

246.speaker: Lileas Graf
246.text: “Mr. Lancea has a point. We have seen it happen many times.”

247.speaker: Deivid Wisci
247.text: “As I was just saying before I was interrupted...”

248.speaker: Symon Holl
248.text: ...of this insane fucking trade war between Arcasia and United Contana!”

249.speaker: Symon Holl
249.text: “...after our entire fucking stock market went down the tubes!"

276.speaker: Lileas Graf
276.text: "I wouldn't worry about that too much. With how Wehlen is dealing with the Bludish terrorists, I would argue that President Smolak would beg us to tighten our immigration."

277.speaker: Lileas Graf
277.text: "With that said, I don't fancy Wehlen as a partner since they are as reliable as a flopping fish out of water."
